checks.label: Screen 2: the motor's starting impedance is 630 ÷ 600 = 1.05 per unit, so 1.05 ÷ (1.05 + 0.15) = 87.5% is left at once; empty until Start, its still reads At once 87.5 with the others –
Screen 3 lights the AVR before Start; once answered, the start runs to its end
Screen 4: 600 kVA × 0.4 = 240 kW; the frequency is lowest at 0.3 s, 55.7 Hz; the voltage sags to 83.8%, recovers to 100%, and the motor gets away with 100% torque
Screen 6: at 900 kVA, 82.4% at once and 72.8% at the lowest; the field ceiling reaches only 2.5 ÷ (1 + 1.5 × 900 ÷ 630) = 79.5%, so torque is 63.3%, and from 2 s the motor is red and Stalled
Screen 8: star-delta takes 600 ÷ 3 = 200 kVA, leaving 95.5% at once; the soft starter takes 300 kVA, leaving 93.3%, lowest 91.4%
Screen 10: two sets halve the reactance the motor sees, so 600 kVA leaves 1.05 ÷ (1.05 + 0.075) = 93.3%, a 6.7% drop instead of 12.5%, and the frequency dips half as far
Screens 5, 9 and 11 show ? for At once until checked; checked, they run 900 kVA DOL on one set (82.4%), star-delta (93.3%) and with the second set on (90.3%)
Screen 7 shows ? for Torque until checked, then 63.3; screen 12 shows only the frequency, its lowest ? until checked, then 55.7 Hz
Screen 13 draws sets A and B, both on the board, with no traces
Starting current is typically six times a motor's rated full-load current, and stays high until about 75% of rated speed: 6 × 100 A = 600 A on screen 1
With a sudden step the voltage drop equals what it would be with no AVR present: the first instant reads 87.5% whatever the AVR's field ceiling, and only later does the AVR lift it
When the engine slows under the frequency dip, the alternator's voltage dip increases: at 600 kVA the lowest is 83.8%, below the 87.5% the AVR's pull alone never falls under
If the voltage recovers to at least 90% of rated, the motor develops 81% of rated torque: 0.9 × 0.9 = 0.81; on one set a DOL start gets away from 700 kVA (93.8%) but stalls at 750 kVA (89.7%)
At every setting the lowest voltage comes before 1 s, so the Lowest tile, filled at 1 s, shows the trace's lowest; a second set always leaves more voltage
Thirteen screens, five that show and eight to try; both picks' answers are second in their lists
